newsitem.title: GREECE: Clashes mark Greek seamen's strike, no injuries.
newsitem.headline: Clashes mark Greek seamen's strike, no injuries.

text.p: Striking Greek seamen clashed with special coast guard forces on Saturday when they tried to stop a passenger ferry from sailing but no one was hurt, the Greek coast guard said.
The walkout has kept most ships with Greek crews idle at ports for six days. Hundreds of trucks are lined up waiting for ferries to sail.

Greek television showed clashes at the port of Kilini in the Peloponnese between special coast guard forces and about 20 seamen trying to stop a passenger ferry from sailing. The coast guard said there were no injuries or arrests.

On the island of Crete, farmers tried unsuccessfully to set fire to mooring lines, demanding that some ships be allowed to transport perishables to the mainland. Tonnes of their produce has been rotting at ports since the strike started.

The Panhellenic Seamen's Federation (PNO), which wants better pensions, benefits and measures against unemployment, on Friday defied a court decision declaring its walkout illegal and said it would end the strike on Tuesday as scheduled.
A Piraeus court ordered the seamen to return to work or face fines and arrest. Police said there had been no detentions so far.

"The court ruling will not affect our movement. It will strengthen the seamen's reaction against the government and the conflict between the two will become sharper," union spokesman George Maroulakis said.
